ingredients.intro: One botanical, one Latin name, and a label that stops sooner than it should. Here is the plant, the fruit the common name refers to, and the two figures the listing leaves out.

cards.alt: Vitex agnus-castus in flower, long spikes of small lilac flowers above palmate leaves
cards.p: A deciduous shrub or small tree of the Mediterranean and western Asia, at home on riverbanks and on dry stony ground. The leaves are palmate, five to seven narrow leaflets fanning out from one point and grey underneath. In late summer it throws long spikes of small lilac flowers, which is when you can place it from a passing car.

cards.alt: Small dark berries of Vitex agnus-castus on the stem
cards.p: The fruit follows the flower: small, hard, dark when ripe, about the size of a peppercorn. That dried fruit is what the trade sells under this name. Our listing prints the species and not the part of it, so the sheet below does not state a part, and the photograph is of the plant rather than of our material.

cards.alt: Clove buds, black peppercorns and a pale flecked powder in three small bowls on a wooden sill, a generated scene
cards.p: The listing prints a capsule count, a serving and a pack weight, and no milligrams a capsule. Without that figure there is no strength on the sheet and no way to compare a capsule of ours with a capsule of anybody else's. The bowls in the picture are a generated scene and none of the powder in them is ours.

cards.alt: Two plain capsules on a saucer beside a glass of water, a generated scene
cards.p: The listing prints 50 vegan capsules. It does not say what the shell is made from, so the sheet does not name a material. The capsules in the picture are a generated scene rather than a photograph of ours.

doctrine.h3: We publish the specification. We do not publish claims about what it does.
doctrine.p: The species is named in Latin, the count and the serving are printed, and the two figures we do not have, the milligrams and the part of the plant, are named as missing rather than guessed at. What chasteberry does in a person is not something we are permitted to say, so it is not on this page, and it is not hinted at either. The live listing says a great deal more than this one does. That is one of the reasons this rebuild exists.

reiss.label: Reiss's turn
reiss.h2: Why this is a short sheet for a well documented plant
paras: This is the page where I have the least to print, and it is not because the plant is obscure. Vitex agnus-castus has been in European herbals for centuries and it is one of the better studied botanicals in the shop. The trouble is the gap between what is known about a plant and what a shop is allowed to write on a shelf card next to a jar of it. Nearly everything I could tell you about this one sits on the far side of that line, so it stays off the page.

What is left is a species, a count, a serving and a set of blanks. Fifty capsules. Two in the morning before breakfast. Twenty five days, then five off. No milligrams, because the label does not carry them. No part of the plant named, because the label does not carry that either. On a herb this well documented, both of those are label problems rather than sourcing problems, and both are on my list for the reprint.

One thing I will say plainly, because it is a caution and not a claim. This is not a herb to start on your own while you are taking something else on prescription. The interactions are documented, the list is not a short one, and a pharmacist can read through it with you in a minute at a counter. Ask first. If the answer comes back no, the twenty five pounds stays in your pocket, and that is the better result of the two.
